 11597	// whatever path prefix reaches them; `.spawn(` also catches a builder. The
 11598	// product crates spawn no processes today, so the over-match is a refusal
 11599	// that names its line, never a miss.
 11600	const CONCURRENCY_EXECUTION_PRIMITIVES: [&str; 12] = [
 11601	    // Blind pass 1 at 5fb1b57 (A06): the list was Rust-shaped, so a thread
 11602	    // created through libc named nothing.
 11603	    "pthread_create",
 11604	    "libc::clone",
 11605	    "clone3",
 11606	    // Blind pass 1 at aa00d41 (A06): the trailing parenthesis meant
 11607	    // `let f = thread::spawn;` named no token while spawning all the same.
 11608	    // A mention of the symbol is the signal; calling it is not required.
 11609	    "::spawn",
 11610	    ".spawn",
 11611	    "::scope",
 11612	    "thread::Builder",
 11613	    "tokio::",
 11614	    "rayon::",
 11615	    "async fn",
 11616	    "crossbeam",
 11617	    "mpsc::",
 11618	];
 11619	/// Tokens that mean code is written to be shared: recorded, not refused.
 11620	const CONCURRENCY_SYNC_PRIMITIVES: [&str; 3] = ["Mutex<", "RwLock<", "Atomic"];

 11627	/// Scan the implementation crates' non-test sources for concurrency
 11628	/// primitives. A file's trailing `#[cfg(test)]` module is skipped; comment
 11629	/// lines are skipped. Deterministic order: crates, files and lines sorted.
 11630	fn scan_concurrency_primitives(root: &Utf8Path) -> Result<ConcurrencyScan> {
 11631	    fn walk(dir: &Utf8Path, out: &mut Vec<Utf8PathBuf>) -> Result<()> {
 11632	        let mut entries = fs::read_dir(dir.as_std_path())
 11633	            .with_context(|| format!("read {dir}"))?
 11634	            .map(|entry| entry.map(|e| e.path()))
 11635	            .collect::<std::io::Result<Vec<_>>>()?;
 11636	        entries.sort();
 11637	        for path in entries {
 11638	            let path = Utf8PathBuf::from_path_buf(path)
 11639	                .map_err(|p| anyhow::anyhow!("non-UTF-8 path {}", p.display()))?;
 11640	            if path.is_dir() {
 11641	                walk(&path, out)?;
 11642	            } else if path.extension() == Some("rs") {
 11643	                out.push(path);
 11644	            }
 11645	        }
 11646	        Ok(())
 11647	    }
 11648	    let mut scan = ConcurrencyScan {
 11649	        execution: Vec::new(),
 11650	        sync: Vec::new(),
 11651	    };
 11652	    let crates_dir = root.join("crates");
 11653	    let mut crate_dirs = fs::read_dir(crates_dir.as_std_path())
 11654	        .with_context(|| format!("read {crates_dir}"))?
 11655	        .map(|entry| entry.map(|e| e.path()))
 11656	        .collect::<std::io::Result<Vec<_>>>()?;
 11657	    crate_dirs.sort();
 11658	    for member in crate_dirs {
 11659	        let member_dir = Utf8PathBuf::from_path_buf(member)
 11660	            .map_err(|p| anyhow::anyhow!("non-UTF-8 path {}", p.display()))?;
 11661	        let Some(name) = member_dir.file_name() else {
 11662	            continue;
 11663	        };
 11664	        if CONCURRENCY_SCAN_EXCLUDED_CRATES.contains(&name) || !member_dir.join("src").is_dir() {
 11665	            continue;
 11666	        }
 11667	        let manifest = member_dir.join("Cargo.toml");
 11668	        if manifest.is_file() {
 11669	            let external = runtime_external_dependencies(&manifest)?;
 11670	            let unknown = external
 11671	                .iter()
 11672	                .filter(|dep| !CONCURRENCY_SCAN_ALLOWED_DEPENDENCIES.contains(&dep.as_str()))
 11673	                .cloned()
 11674	                .collect::<Vec<_>>();
 11675	            anyhow::ensure!(
 11676	                unknown.is_empty(),
 11677	                "{name} depends on {unknown:?}, outside the closed list the \
 11678	                 concurrency scan reasons about; a dependency may export a \
 11679	                 macro that spawns, which a lexical scan cannot see. Decide, \
 11680	                 then widen CONCURRENCY_SCAN_ALLOWED_DEPENDENCIES"
 11681	            );
 11682	        }
 11683	        let mut files = Vec::new();
 11684	        walk(&member_dir.join("src"), &mut files)?;
 11685	        for file in files {
 11686	            let text = fs::read_to_string(&file).with_context(|| format!("read {file}"))?;
 11687	            let relative = file.strip_prefix(root).unwrap_or(&file);
 11688	            // Blind pass 1 at 612cbcc (A06): this used to stop at the first
 11689	            // `#[cfg(test)]` line, so production code after an earlier test
 11690	            // module escaped the scan. The attributed item is skipped as a
 11691	            // block (brace depth) or, for a brace-less item, through its `;`,
 11692	            // and scanning resumes after it. F-56: braces used to be
 11693	            // counted textually, strings and comments included, so an
 11694	            // unbalanced brace inside a test module could end the skip late
 11695	            // and hide a production spawn. Only structural braces count now,
 11696	            // the same scanner the mutant anchor screen uses.
 11697	            let mut skipping: Option<(usize, bool)> = None;
 11698	            let mut scanner = SourceScanner::default();
 11699	            for (index, line) in text.lines().enumerate() {
 11700	                let trimmed = line.trim();
 11701	                let structural = scanner.structural(line);
 11702	                if let Some((depth, entered)) = skipping.as_mut() {
 11703	                    *depth += structural.matches('{').count();
 11704	                    let closes = structural.matches('}').count();
 11705	                    if *depth > 0 {
 11706	                        *entered = true;
 11707	                    }
 11708	                    *depth = depth.saturating_sub(closes);
 11709	                    if (*entered && *depth == 0) || (!*entered && trimmed.ends_with(';')) {
 11710	                        skipping = None;
 11711	                    }
 11712	                    continue;
 11713	                }
 11714	                if trimmed.replace(' ', "") == "#[cfg(test)]" {
 11715	                    skipping = Some((0, false));
 11716	                    continue;
 11717	                }
 11718	                if trimmed.starts_with("//") {
 11719	                    continue;
 11720	                }
 11721	                for token in CONCURRENCY_EXECUTION_PRIMITIVES {
 11722	                    if line.contains(token) {
 11723	                        scan.execution
 11724	                            .push(format!("{relative}:{}:{token}", index + 1));
 11725	                    }
 11726	                }
 11727	                for token in CONCURRENCY_SYNC_PRIMITIVES {
 11728	                    if line.contains(token) {
 11729	                        scan.sync.push(format!("{relative}:{}:{token}", index + 1));
 11730	                    }
 11731	                }
 11732	            }
 11733	        }
 11734	    }
 11735	    Ok(scan)
 11736	}

  3763	            let Ok(count) = count.parse::<usize>() else {
  3764	                return false;
  3765	            };
  3766	            count > 0 && target_line >= start && target_line.saturating_sub(start) < count

 11562	/// The external crates `manifest` depends on at run time, workspace members
 11563	/// excluded. Dev-dependencies are excluded too: the scan reads `src/` only,
 11564	/// which a dev-dependency cannot reach.
 11565	fn runtime_external_dependencies(manifest: &Utf8Path) -> Result<BTreeSet<String>> {
 11566	    let text = fs::read_to_string(manifest).with_context(|| format!("read {manifest}"))?;
 11567	    let mut section = String::new();
 11568	    let mut out = BTreeSet::new();
 11569	    for line in text.lines() {
 11570	        let trimmed = line.trim();
 11571	        if let Some(name) = trimmed.strip_prefix('[').and_then(|r| r.strip_suffix(']')) {
 11572	            section.clear();
 11573	            section.push_str(name);
 11574	            continue;
 11575	        }
 11576	        let last = section.rsplit('.').next().unwrap_or_default();
 11577	        if last != "dependencies" || section.contains("dev-") || section.contains("build-") {
 11578	            continue;
 11579	        }
 11580	        let Some((key, _)) = trimmed.split_once('=') else {
 11581	            continue;
 11582	        };
 11583	        let key = key.trim().trim_matches('"');
 11584	        // `serde.workspace = true` names the crate before the dot.
 11585	        let key = key.split('.').next().unwrap_or(key);
 11586	        if key.is_empty() || key.starts_with('#') || key.starts_with("liminal") {
 11587	            continue;
 11588	        }
 11589	        out.insert(key.to_owned());
 11590	    }
 11591	    Ok(out)
 11592	}

 11597	// whatever path prefix reaches them; `.spawn(` also catches a builder. The
 11598	// product crates spawn no processes today, so the over-match is a refusal
 11599	// that names its line, never a miss.
 11600	const CONCURRENCY_EXECUTION_PRIMITIVES: [&str; 12] = [
 11601	    // Blind pass 1 at 5fb1b57 (A06): the list was Rust-shaped, so a thread
 11602	    // created through libc named nothing.
 11603	    "pthread_create",
 11604	    "libc::clone",
 11605	    "clone3",
 11606	    // Blind pass 1 at aa00d41 (A06): the trailing parenthesis meant
 11607	    // `let f = thread::spawn;` named no token while spawning all the same.
 11608	    // A mention of the symbol is the signal; calling it is not required.
 11609	    "::spawn",
 11610	    ".spawn",
 11611	    "::scope",
 11612	    "thread::Builder",
 11613	    "tokio::",
 11614	    "rayon::",
 11615	    "async fn",
 11616	    "crossbeam",
 11617	    "mpsc::",
 11618	];
 11619	/// Tokens that mean code is written to be shared: recorded, not refused.
 11620	const CONCURRENCY_SYNC_PRIMITIVES: [&str; 3] = ["Mutex<", "RwLock<", "Atomic"];

 11627	/// Scan the implementation crates' non-test sources for concurrency
 11628	/// primitives. A file's trailing `#[cfg(test)]` module is skipped; comment
 11629	/// lines are skipped. Deterministic order: crates, files and lines sorted.
 11630	fn scan_concurrency_primitives(root: &Utf8Path) -> Result<ConcurrencyScan> {
 11631	    fn walk(dir: &Utf8Path, out: &mut Vec<Utf8PathBuf>) -> Result<()> {
 11632	        let mut entries = fs::read_dir(dir.as_std_path())
 11633	            .with_context(|| format!("read {dir}"))?
 11634	            .map(|entry| entry.map(|e| e.path()))
 11635	            .collect::<std::io::Result<Vec<_>>>()?;
 11636	        entries.sort();
 11637	        for path in entries {
 11638	            let path = Utf8PathBuf::from_path_buf(path)
 11639	                .map_err(|p| anyhow::anyhow!("non-UTF-8 path {}", p.display()))?;
 11640	            if path.is_dir() {
 11641	                walk(&path, out)?;
 11642	            } else if path.extension() == Some("rs") {
 11643	                out.push(path);
 11644	            }
 11645	        }
 11646	        Ok(())
 11647	    }
 11648	    let mut scan = ConcurrencyScan {
 11649	        execution: Vec::new(),
 11650	        sync: Vec::new(),
 11651	    };
 11652	    let crates_dir = root.join("crates");
 11653	    let mut crate_dirs = fs::read_dir(crates_dir.as_std_path())
 11654	        .with_context(|| format!("read {crates_dir}"))?
 11655	        .map(|entry| entry.map(|e| e.path()))
 11656	        .collect::<std::io::Result<Vec<_>>>()?;
 11657	    crate_dirs.sort();
 11658	    for member in crate_dirs {
 11659	        let member_dir = Utf8PathBuf::from_path_buf(member)
 11660	            .map_err(|p| anyhow::anyhow!("non-UTF-8 path {}", p.display()))?;
 11661	        let Some(name) = member_dir.file_name() else {
 11662	            continue;
 11663	        };
 11664	        if CONCURRENCY_SCAN_EXCLUDED_CRATES.contains(&name) || !member_dir.join("src").is_dir() {
 11665	            continue;
 11666	        }
 11667	        let manifest = member_dir.join("Cargo.toml");
 11668	        if manifest.is_file() {
 11669	            let external = runtime_external_dependencies(&manifest)?;
 11670	            let unknown = external
 11671	                .iter()
 11672	                .filter(|dep| !CONCURRENCY_SCAN_ALLOWED_DEPENDENCIES.contains(&dep.as_str()))
 11673	                .cloned()
 11674	                .collect::<Vec<_>>();
 11675	            anyhow::ensure!(
 11676	                unknown.is_empty(),
 11677	                "{name} depends on {unknown:?}, outside the closed list the \
 11678	                 concurrency scan reasons about; a dependency may export a \
 11679	                 macro that spawns, which a lexical scan cannot see. Decide, \
 11680	                 then widen CONCURRENCY_SCAN_ALLOWED_DEPENDENCIES"
 11681	            );
 11682	        }
 11683	        let mut files = Vec::new();
 11684	        walk(&member_dir.join("src"), &mut files)?;
 11685	        for file in files {
 11686	            let text = fs::read_to_string(&file).with_context(|| format!("read {file}"))?;
 11687	            let relative = file.strip_prefix(root).unwrap_or(&file);
 11688	            // Blind pass 1 at 612cbcc (A06): this used to stop at the first
 11689	            // `#[cfg(test)]` line, so production code after an earlier test
 11690	            // module escaped the scan. The attributed item is skipped as a
 11691	            // block (brace depth) or, for a brace-less item, through its `;`,
 11692	            // and scanning resumes after it. F-56: braces used to be
 11693	            // counted textually, strings and comments included, so an
 11694	            // unbalanced brace inside a test module could end the skip late
 11695	            // and hide a production spawn. Only structural braces count now,
 11696	            // the same scanner the mutant anchor screen uses.
 11697	            let mut skipping: Option<(usize, bool)> = None;
 11698	            let mut scanner = SourceScanner::default();
 11699	            for (index, line) in text.lines().enumerate() {
 11700	                let trimmed = line.trim();
 11701	                let structural = scanner.structural(line);
 11702	                if let Some((depth, entered)) = skipping.as_mut() {
 11703	                    *depth += structural.matches('{').count();
 11704	                    let closes = structural.matches('}').count();
 11705	                    if *depth > 0 {
 11706	                        *entered = true;
 11707	                    }
 11708	                    *depth = depth.saturating_sub(closes);
 11709	                    if (*entered && *depth == 0) || (!*entered && trimmed.ends_with(';')) {
 11710	                        skipping = None;
 11711	                    }
 11712	                    continue;
 11713	                }
 11714	                if trimmed.replace(' ', "") == "#[cfg(test)]" {
 11715	                    skipping = Some((0, false));
 11716	                    continue;
 11717	                }
 11718	                if trimmed.starts_with("//") {
 11719	                    continue;
 11720	                }
 11721	                for token in CONCURRENCY_EXECUTION_PRIMITIVES {
 11722	                    if line.contains(token) {
 11723	                        scan.execution
 11724	                            .push(format!("{relative}:{}:{token}", index + 1));
 11725	                    }
 11726	                }
 11727	                for token in CONCURRENCY_SYNC_PRIMITIVES {
 11728	                    if line.contains(token) {
 11729	                        scan.sync.push(format!("{relative}:{}:{token}", index + 1));
 11730	                    }
 11731	                }
 11732	            }
 11733	        }
 11734	    }
 11735	    Ok(scan)
 11736	}

  3462	    root: &Utf8Path,

  3468	        return Ok(());
  3469	    }

  3471	        format!(
  3472	            "{who}: resolved finding attempt {:?} has no resolution proof",
  3473	            attempt.id

  3475	    })?;
  3476	    require_git_object_id(&format!("{who} resolution commit"), &resolution.commit)?;
  3477	    let fixed_oid = git_text(root, &["rev-parse", &fixed_base.commit])?;

  3480	        fixed_oid != resolution_oid,
  3481	        "{who}: resolution commit must be a strict descendant of fixed base"
  3482	    );

  3484	        format!(
  3485	            "{who}: resolution commit {} is not a descendant of fixed base {}",
  3486	            resolution.commit, fixed_base.commit
  3487	        )
  3488	    })?;

  3490	        format!(
  3491	            "{who}: resolution commit {} is not reachable from current qualification HEAD",
  3492	            resolution.commit
  3493	        )
  3494	    })?;
  3495	    let evidence_path = safe_repo_path(root, &resolution.evidence_path, who)?;
  3496	    let evidence_bytes = fs::read(&evidence_path)
  3497	        .with_context(|| format!("{evidence_path}: resolution evidence is missing"))?;
  3498	    let evidence_text = String::from_utf8_lossy(&evidence_bytes);

  3500	        evidence_text.contains(&attempt.id)
  3501	            && evidence_text.contains(&attempt.target)
  3502	            && evidence_text.contains(&resolution.coordinate),
  3503	        "{who}: resolution evidence must name attempted finding {}, target {}, and fix coordinate {}",

  3505	        attempt.target,
  3506	        resolution.coordinate
  3507	    );

  3509	        evidence_text
  3510	            .lines()
  3511	            .any(|line| line.trim() == "resolution_result: pass")
  3512	            && evidence_text
  3513	                .lines()
  3514	                .any(|line| line.trim_start().starts_with("verification_command:"))
  3515	            && evidence_text
  3516	                .lines()

  3519	    );

  3524	    require_eq(
  3525	        "resolution evidence_sha256",
  3526	        &resolution.evidence_sha256,
  3527	        &digest,
  3528	    )?;
  3529	    let committed_bytes = git_blob(root, &resolution.commit, &resolution.evidence_path)
  3530	        .with_context(|| {
  3531	            format!(
  3532	                "{who}: resolution evidence {} is absent at commit {}",
  3533	                resolution.evidence_path, resolution.commit
  3534	            )
  3535	        })?;
  3536	    let mut committed_hasher = Sha256::new();
  3537	    committed_hasher.update(&committed_bytes);

  3540	        "resolution committed evidence_sha256",
  3541	        &resolution.evidence_sha256,
  3542	        &committed_digest,
  3543	    )?;

  3545	        !resolution.coordinate.trim().is_empty(),
  3546	        "{who}: resolved finding attempt {:?} has empty fix coordinate",
  3547	        attempt.id
  3548	    );

  3550	        &format!("{who} resolution evidence_sha256"),

  3554	        .coordinate
  3555	        .rsplit_once(':')
  3556	        .with_context(|| format!("{who}: resolution coordinate must be file:line"))?;

  3558	        .target
  3559	        .rsplit_once(':')
  3560	        .map(|(file, _)| file)

  3563	        coordinate_file == target_file,

  3568	        .with_context(|| format!("{who}: resolution coordinate line is not numeric"))?;

  3578	    );

  3581	        "{who}: resolution coordinate may not name locked acceptance corpus"
  3582	    );

  3584	        root,
  3585	        &["show", &format!("{}:{coordinate_file}", resolution.commit)],
  3586	    )?;
  3587	    anyhow::ensure!(
  3588	        line <= source.lines().count().max(1),
  3589	        "{who}: resolution coordinate line {line} is outside {coordinate_file}"
  3590	    );

  3592	        root,
  3593	        &fixed_base.commit,
  3594	        &resolution.commit,
  3595	        who,
  3596	        coordinate_file,
  3597	        line,
  3598	    )?;
  3599	    Ok(())
  3600	}

  3652	        .collect::<BTreeMap<_, _>>();

  3664	            .with_context(|| format!("{who}: finding {id:?} has no non-empty attempt_id"))?;

  3746	fn diff_contains_added_line(diff: &str, target_line: usize) -> bool {
  3747	    diff.lines()
  3748	        .filter(|line| line.starts_with("@@ "))
  3749	        .any(|header| {
  3750	            let Some(range) = header
  3751	                .split_whitespace()
  3752	                .find(|token| token.starts_with('+'))
  3753	                .and_then(|token| token.strip_prefix('+'))
  3754	            else {
  3755	                return false;
  3756	            };
  3757	            let (start, count) = range
  3758	                .split_once(',')
  3759	                .map_or((range, "1"), |(start, count)| (start, count));
  3760	            let Ok(start) = start.parse::<usize>() else {
  3761	                return false;
  3762	            };
  3763	            let Ok(count) = count.parse::<usize>() else {
  3764	                return false;
  3765	            };
  3766	            count > 0 && target_line >= start && target_line.saturating_sub(start) < count
  3767	        })
  3768	}

 11565	fn runtime_external_dependencies(manifest: &Utf8Path) -> Result<BTreeSet<String>> {
 11566	    let text = fs::read_to_string(manifest).with_context(|| format!("read {manifest}"))?;

 11568	    let mut out = BTreeSet::new();
 11569	    for line in text.lines() {
 11570	        let trimmed = line.trim();
 11571	        if let Some(name) = trimmed.strip_prefix('[').and_then(|r| r.strip_suffix(']')) {
 11572	            section.clear();
 11573	            section.push_str(name);
 11574	            continue;
 11575	        }

 11577	        if last != "dependencies" || section.contains("dev-") || section.contains("build-") {
 11578	            continue;
 11579	        }

 11581	            continue;
 11582	        };
 11583	        let key = key.trim().trim_matches('"');

 11585	        let key = key.split('.').next().unwrap_or(key);
 11586	        if key.is_empty() || key.starts_with('#') || key.starts_with("liminal") {

 13820	/// itself, so `ComponentDeps` is never its own oracle.

 13822	fn case_invalidation(rng: &mut Rng) -> Result<Case> {

 13824	        BasisComponent, BasisPerspective, CausalFrontier, ComponentDeps, WorkspaceBasis,
 13825	    };

 13827	    let category = rng.category("Basis/revision/query invalidation");
 13828	    let perspective = match category {
 13829	        "client-scoped" => BasisPerspective::ClientScoped {
 13830	            client: liminal_id::ClientId::from_uuid(rng.uuid()),
 13831	        },
 13832	        "published" => BasisPerspective::Published {
 13833	            revision: liminal_id::PublicationId::from_uuid(rng.uuid()),
 13834	        },
 13835	        "federated" => BasisPerspective::Federated {
 13836	            domain: liminal_id::FederationId::from_uuid(rng.uuid()),
 13837	            frontier: CausalFrontier(vec![
 13838	                u8::try_from(rng.below(255)).expect("frontier byte fits"),
 13839	            ]),
 13840	        },
 13841	        _ => BasisPerspective::DurableOnly,
 13842	    };
 13843	    let basis = WorkspaceBasis {
 13844	        transaction: liminal_id::TransactionId::from_uuid(rng.uuid()),
 13845	        perspective,
 13846	        components: if category == "empty-basis" {
 13847	            BTreeMap::new()
 13848	        } else {
 13849	            BTreeMap::from([(
 13850	                liminal_revision::graph_key(),
 13851	                BasisComponent::GraphSnapshot {
 13852	                    revision: liminal_id::GraphRevisionId(rng.below(10_000)),
 13853	                },
 13854	            )])
 13855	        },
 13856	    };
 13857	    let basis_witness = serde_json::to_vec(&basis)?;
 13858	    let malformed = matches!(
 13859	        category,
 13860	        "truncated" | "hostile" | "invalid-token" | "unknown-perspective"
 13861	    );
 13862	    // Target the declared domain (computations that read >=1 component) and
 13863	    // keep a rare out-of-domain probe so the discard path stays exercised.
 13864	    let read_count = if category == "empty-basis" || rng.below(384) == 0 {
 13865	        0
 13866	    } else {
 13867	        1 + rng.below(5)
 13868	    };
 13869	    let mut deps = ComponentDeps::default();
 13870	    let mut expected = BTreeSet::new();
 13871	    for _ in 0..read_count {
 13872	        let key = liminal_id::JurisdictionKey::Path(liminal_id::PathId(
 13873	            format!("{category}/{}", rng.word()).into(),
 13874	        ));
 13875	        deps.record(key.clone());
 13876	        expected.insert(key);
 13877	    }
 13878	    if malformed {
 13879	        let key = liminal_id::JurisdictionKey::Path(liminal_id::PathId(
 13880	            format!("{category}/__haqp_negative").into(),
 13881	        ));
 13882	        deps.record(key.clone());
 13883	        let invalidated = deps.invalidated_by(&key);
 13884	        let raw = match category {
 13885	            "truncated" => b"{".to_vec(),
 13886	            "hostile" => vec![0xff, 0x00, 0x7f],
 13887	            "invalid-token" => br#"{"perspective":"unknown"}"#.to_vec(),
 13888	            "unknown-perspective" => br#"{"perspective":{"future":true}}"#.to_vec(),
 13889	            _ => unreachable!("malformed invalidation category {category}"),
 13890	        };
 13891	        anyhow::ensure!(
 13892	            serde_json::from_slice::<WorkspaceBasis>(&raw).is_err(),
 13893	            "invalidation malformed category {category} unexpectedly decoded"
 13894	        );
 13895	        return Ok(Case::Negative {
 13896	            category,
 13897	            witness: [
 13898	                format!("basis-negative:{category}:{invalidated:?}:").into_bytes(),
 13899	                raw,
 13900	                basis_witness,
 13901	            ]
 13902	            .concat(),
 13903	        });
 13904	    }
 13905	    // Out of domain: nothing was read, so invalidation is vacuous.
 13906	    if expected.is_empty() {
 13907	        return Ok(Case::Negative {
 13908	            category,
 13909	            witness: [b"vacuous-invalidation:".to_vec(), basis_witness].concat(),
 13910	        });
 13911	    }
 13912	
 13913	    // Select a negative witness outside the generated read set. A random
 13914	    // `unread/<word>` can collide with a legitimate read key, making the only
 13915	    // negative assertion disappear exactly when the generator hits that case.
 13916	    let unrelated = (0..u32::MAX)
 13917	        .map(|index| {
 13918	            liminal_id::JurisdictionKey::Path(liminal_id::PathId(
 13919	                format!("unread/__haqp_negative_{index}").into(),
 13920	            ))
 13921	        })
 13922	        .find(|candidate| !expected.contains(candidate))
 13923	        .expect("finite generated read set leaves a negative witness");

 13925	        format!("extra/{category}/__haqp_0").into(),
 13926	    ));
 13927	    anyhow::ensure!(
 13928	        !expected.contains(&extra),
 13929	        "extra dependency key collided with generated read set"
 13930	    );

 13932	        independent_oracle_source_invalidation(&mut deps, &expected, &unrelated, &extra)?;
 13933	    witness.extend_from_slice(&basis_witness);
 13934	    Ok(Case::Accepted { category, witness })
 13935	}

 13940	/// Run the five HAQP generated-evidence families with MEASURED acceptance.
 13941	///

 13943	/// candidate itself, and checks at least one metamorphic relation that does
 13944	/// not route through the implementation's own equality path. Counts are
 13945	/// tallied from outcomes — never echoed from the requested case count
 13946	/// (M17.5 finding F-07).
 13947	pub fn run_generated_repo(root: &Utf8Path, cases: u64) -> Result<()> {
 13948	    let (evidence, timings) = generate_evidence(cases)?;
 13949	    let artifact = GeneratedEvidenceArtifact {

 13956	    fs::create_dir_all(path.parent().expect("evidence parent"))?;

 13960	        let rate = row.discards as f64 * 100.0 / row.attempts.max(1) as f64;
 13961	        println!(
 13962	            "{}: {} accepted / {} attempts ({} discarded, {rate:.2}%) in {elapsed_ms}ms",
 13963	            row.family, row.accepted, row.attempts, row.discards
 13964	        );

 13973	/// Run the five families and return their evidence rows plus per-family
 13974	/// wall-clock timings.
 13975	///
 13976	/// The timings are returned SEPARATELY rather than embedded in the rows on
 13977	/// purpose: the rows are the hashable artifact and must be a pure function of
 13978	/// the seed and the code under test, while the timings are telemetry for the
 13979	/// operator (M17.5 pass-2 #18).
 13980	///
 13981	/// The case-count guard is a separate function so its BOUNDARIES are testable:
 13982	/// `>` -> `>=` at the safety limit can only be discriminated by a case that
 13983	/// runs at exactly 10,000,000, which no test can afford. Extracting the
 13984	/// predicate makes the boundary checkable in microseconds (M17.5 F-30).
 13985	/// Reject a case count that is zero or beyond the safety limit.
 13986	fn validate_case_count(cases: u64) -> Result<()> {
 13987	    if cases == 0 {
 13988	        anyhow::bail!("generated case count must be positive");
 13989	    }
 13990	    if cases > 10_000_000 {
 13991	        anyhow::bail!("generated case count exceeds safety limit: {cases} > 10000000");
 13992	    }
 13993	    Ok(())
 13994	}

 13997	    clippy::too_many_lines,
 13998	    reason = "evidence runner keeps deterministic accounting and digest boundaries together"
 13999	)]
 14000	fn generate_evidence(cases: u64) -> Result<(Vec<GeneratedEvidence>, Vec<u64>)> {
 14001	    validate_case_count(cases)?;
 14002	    let families: [Family; 5] = [
 14003	        ("source/CST/formatting", case_source_cst),
 14004	        ("graph/interchange codecs", case_interchange),
 14005	        ("transforms/projections", case_transform),
 14006	        ("repair/ILRP/recovery", case_repair),
 14007	        ("Basis/revision/query invalidation", case_invalidation),
 14008	    ];
 14009	
 14010	    let mut evidence = Vec::new();
 14011	    let mut timings = Vec::new();
 14012	    for (index, (family, run)) in families.into_iter().enumerate() {
 14013	        let seed = 0x9E37_79B9_7F4A_7C15_u64 ^ (index as u64).wrapping_mul(0x0100_0000_01B3);
 14014	        let mut rng = Rng(seed);
 14015	        let started = Instant::now();
 14016	        let mut digest = blake3::Hasher::new();
 14017	        digest.update(&seed.to_le_bytes());
 14018	        // ADR-0020 §4 requires >=100,000 ACCEPTED cases, so run until the
 14019	        // acceptance target is met rather than stopping at N attempts. The
 14020	        // attempt cap keeps a badly-targeted generator from running forever
 14021	        // instead of silently reporting a short campaign.
 14022	        let (mut accepted, mut discards, mut negatives, mut attempts) = (0u64, 0u64, 0u64, 0u64);
 14023	        let mut category_counts = BTreeMap::<String, u64>::new();
 14024	        // Negative categories are exercised inputs, not discards; families
 14025	        // with broad malformed coverage need a larger attempt budget to reach
 14026	        // their accepted floor without silently dropping categories.
 14027	        let attempt_cap = cases.saturating_mul(4);
 14028	        while accepted < cases {
 14029	            anyhow::ensure!(
 14030	                attempts < attempt_cap,
 14031	                "{family}: {attempts} attempts yielded only {accepted}/{cases} accepted \
 14032	                 — the generator is not targeting its declared domain"
 14033	            );
 14034	            attempts += 1;
 14035	            match run(&mut rng).with_context(|| format!("{family} attempt {attempts}"))? {
 14036	                Case::Accepted { category, witness } => {
 14037	                    // A family that witnesses nothing would restore exactly the
 14038	                    // #16 defect: a digest independent of the code under test.
 14039	                    anyhow::ensure!(
 14040	                        !witness.is_empty(),
 14041	                        "{family}: accepted attempt {attempts} with an empty witness, so \
 14042	                         the evidence hash would not depend on what the code produced"
 14043	                    );
 14044	                    accepted += 1;
 14045	                    *category_counts.entry(category.to_owned()).or_default() += 1;
 14046	                    digest.update(b"A");
 14047	                    digest.update(category.as_bytes());
 14048	                    digest.update(&witness);
 14049	                }
 14050	                Case::Discarded { category, witness } => {
 14051	                    anyhow::ensure!(
 14052	                        !witness.is_empty(),
 14053	                        "{family}: discarded attempt {attempts} with an empty witness, so \
 14054	                         the evidence records that something was discarded and not what"
 14055	                    );
 14056	                    discards += 1;
 14057	                    *category_counts.entry(category.to_owned()).or_default() += 1;
 14058	                    digest.update(b"D");
 14059	                    digest.update(category.as_bytes());
 14060	                    digest.update(&witness);
 14061	                }
 14062	                Case::Negative { category, witness } => {
 14063	                    anyhow::ensure!(
 14064	                        !witness.is_empty(),
 14065	                        "{family}: negative attempt {attempts} has an empty witness"
 14066	                    );
 14067	                    negatives += 1;
 14068	                    *category_counts.entry(category.to_owned()).or_default() += 1;
 14069	                    digest.update(b"N");
 14070	                    digest.update(category.as_bytes());
 14071	                    digest.update(&witness);
 14072	                }
 14073	            }
 14074	            // The RNG state binds the INPUT; the witness above binds the OUTPUT.
 14075	            digest.update(&rng.0.to_le_bytes());
 14076	        }
 14077	        anyhow::ensure!(
 14078	            accepted + discards + negatives == attempts,
 14079	            "{family}: accounting lost cases"
 14080	        );
 14081	        let evidence_hash = digest.finalize().to_hex().to_string();
 14082	        let relation_rows = generated_relations(family)
 14083	            .iter()
 14084	            .map(|relation| GeneratedRelationEvidence {
 14085	                relation: (*relation).to_owned(),
 14086	                oracle_id: format!("oracle:{}", family.replace(['/', ' ', '-'], "_")),
 14087	                result: "pass".to_owned(),
 14088	                artifact_blake3: blake3::hash(
 14089	                    format!("{family}\0{relation}\0{evidence_hash}").as_bytes(),
 14090	                )
 14091	                .to_hex()
 14092	                .to_string(),
 14093	            })
 14094	            .collect::<Vec<_>>();
 14095	        let relation_matrix_blake3 = blake3::hash(
 14096	            serde_json::to_vec(&relation_rows)
 14097	                .context("serialize generated relation matrix")?
 14098	                .as_slice(),
 14099	        )
 14100	        .to_hex()
 14101	        .to_string();
 14102	        evidence.push(GeneratedEvidence {
 14103	            family: family.to_owned(),
 14104	            accepted,
 14105	            attempts,
 14106	            discards,
 14107	            negatives,
 14108	            seed,
 14109	            evidence_hash,
 14110	            category_counts,
 14111	            relations: relation_rows,
 14112	            oracle: Some(GeneratedOracleEvidence {
 14113	                id: format!("oracle:{}", family.replace(['/', ' ', '-'], "_")),
 14114	                source: generated_oracle_source(family).to_owned(),
 14115	                independent: true,
 14116	                relation_matrix_blake3,
 14117	            }),
 14118	        });
 14119	        timings.push(u64::try_from(started.elapsed().as_millis()).unwrap_or(u64::MAX));
 14120	    }
 14121	    Ok((evidence, timings))
 14122	}
